tasks.title: Generator: project cards from the Projects section
tasks.body:
Bullets under a `## Projects` heading in the form `**Name**: one-liner` (optionally followed by a link) render as project cards (`<article>` with heading, text and link) instead of a plain list.

Acceptance:
- `parse()` exposes projects as structured items; other sections are unchanged.
- Tests in `scripts/build.test.mjs` cover a project with and without a link.
- The sample `description.md` still builds and `npm run check:site` passes.

tasks.title: Generator: optional front matter for role, location and links
tasks.body:
Support an optional `---` front-matter block at the top of `description.md` with `role`, `location`, `accent` and `links` (label: url). Absent keys change nothing.

Acceptance:
- Dependency-free parsing; unknown keys produce a warning, not a crash.
- Role and location appear in the header; links appear in the header or contact section.
- Tests for: no front matter, partial front matter, unknown key.

tasks.title: Generator: images with required alt text
tasks.body: `![alt](path)` in the description renders an `` and copies the file into `dist/`. A missing file or empty alt fails the build with a line-numbered error. Acceptance: - Tests for a valid image, a missing file and empty alt. - `check:site` passes for a description with one image.

tasks.title: Generator: line-numbered errors for unreadable descriptions
tasks.body:
When the description cannot be rendered well (no name heading, empty section, duplicate section titles), the build exits non-zero with `description.md:<line>: <what to fix>`.

Acceptance:
- Each case has a test asserting the message and line number.
- The sample description builds with no warnings.

tasks.title: Site: design tokens and a professional type scale
tasks.body:
Replace the seed styles with CSS custom properties for a modular type scale, spacing steps and colours (light and dark), and restyle the page with them so it reads as a deliberate, professional portfolio.

Acceptance:
- All sizes, spaces and colours in the CSS come from tokens.
- Looks intentional at 375 px and 1280 px wide, in light and dark (attach screenshots to the PR).
- `npm run check:site` passes; HTML+CSS stays under budget.

tasks.title: Site: responsive project card layout
tasks.body:
Lay out project cards (from the generator task, or the current project list if that has not landed) as a single column on phones and a grid on wide screens, with no horizontal scroll at 320 px.

Acceptance:
- Screenshots at 320, 768 and 1280 px in the PR.
- `npm run check:site` passes.

tasks.title: Site: contrast and heading-order rules in check:site
tasks.body:
Extend `scripts/checks/site.mjs` so it fails when heading levels skip (h1 to h3) and when the text/background and accent/background token pairs fall below WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) in either colour scheme.

Acceptance:
- Rules stay dependency-free.
- A negative test (a broken copy of the page) shows each new rule failing; paste the output in the PR.
- The current site passes, or the PR fixes it so it does.

tasks.title: Site: Open Graph tags and a favicon from the description
tasks.body:
Emit `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:type` and a simple generated SVG favicon (initials on the accent colour), all derived from the description.

Acceptance:
- No new fields are required in `description.md`.
- `check:site` verifies the favicon file exists and the OG tags are non-empty.

tasks.title: UI: show the built portfolio on the dashboard home
tasks.body:
Make `swarm-ui` `/` show the current built portfolio (an embedded preview or a clear link to it) alongside the swarm's status, so visitors see the product and its makers together.

Acceptance:
- Works when swarm memory is unreachable (shows the product, hides live stats).
- `npm --prefix swarm-ui run build` passes.

tasks.title: UI: theme the dashboard with the portfolio tokens
tasks.body:
Set `theme.cssVars` in `swarm-ui/app/swarm/swarm.config.ts` so the dashboard's accent, background and text colours match the portfolio's tokens in light and dark.

Acceptance:
- Only `swarm.config.ts` (and at most `swarm.css` variables) change.
- Screenshots in light and dark in the PR; `npm --prefix swarm-ui run build` passes.
